originality.rationale: The local four-cycle-only component theorem and sharp dimension-four frozen-matching transition are not implied by published Hamiltonian-cycle-union connectivity (Fink), longer-cycle dimer ergodicity (Hartarsky–Lichev–Toninelli), or a complete-graph XOR-difference matching census. Existing Q4 matching counts and an accessible forcing polynomial study are explicitly excluded as originality claims. Targeted searches and direct full-text checks support a best-knowledge distinction, with the risk of unindexed prior equivalent computations acknowledged.
residual_risks: A differently indexed paper/code repository may have enumerated D_2(Q4) or implicitly included a parity-slice construction.

Published descriptions of local dimer dynamics in three-dimensional shapes demonstrate related frozen phenomena, so the substantive novelty is the exact unit-hypercube threshold plus quantitative classification and infinite lower bound, not the existence of frozen dimers in all settings.

value.rationale: The natural question of exact reachability under the smallest local dimer operation has a sharp freezing threshold at dimension four, complete first-exceptional component geometry, and an explicit doubly exponential family of higher-dimensional frozen states. This is a structural theorem with a clear distinction from existing long-cycle ergodicity or global Hamiltonian-union dynamics; it is not merely a known matching census or routine parameter substitution.
